title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Maria Chen
body:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and commonly used internal templates. Its goal is to provide a single reference for employees, managers, and process owners to ensure consistent, auditable, and secure operations.

Scope:
These policies apply to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors who access Redwood systems or data, participate in company procurement, or travel on behalf of the company. Exceptions require documented approval from the owner_team and either Security or Finance as appropriate.

1) Roles and ownership (high level)
- Document owner: people-ops (Maria Chen) — responsible for maintenance and publishing.
- Security owner (RBAC, account hygiene): Security team (Priya Desai).
- Change management owner (CAB): Eng Platform (Ethan Williams).
- Procurement and vendor owner: Finance & Legal (Alejandro Ruiz).
- Travel policy owner: People Ops (Maria Chen) + Finance.
- Audit and compliance: Security & Compliance.

For any procedure below, the named owner is responsible for updates, training, and auditing.

2) Access & permissions
Principles:
- Principle of least privilege (PoLP): Grant the minimum permissions required for tasks.
- Time-bound access for contractors and temporary projects.
- All privileged access requires MFA and hardware-backed keys where supported.

Access request process (standard requests) — SLA: 3 business days
1. Submit an access request via the Access Request Form (Confluence link / internal form). Provide: resource, reason, duration, manager approval.
2. Manager reviews and approves in the request system.
3. Resource owner (service owner) reviews and approves.
4. On approval, IAM automation provisions access; request marked complete and logged.

Emergency (break-glass) access — SLA: immediate with post-hoc review
1. Emergency access requires pager/on-call escalation to the service owner.
2. Temporary elevated access is granted for up to 4 hours and automatically revoked.
3. Post-incident, requestor must submit a retrospective within 48 hours; Security will perform an audit.

Periodic review and revocation:
- Quarterly access reviews for privileged groups (admins, infra, database access).
- Contractors: access expiration aligned to contract end date.
- IAM logs retained per Data Management policy.

Approval matrix (examples):
- < $1,000 SaaS subscription: Team Lead approval.
- $1,000–$25,000: Department Head + Procurement intake.
- > $25,000: Finance Director + Legal + Procurement Committee.

3) Change management
Purpose: Minimize risk of service disruption while enabling rapid delivery.
Change types:
- Standard change: pre-approved, low risk (routine backups, config tweaks). No CAB required.
- Normal change: requires approval by Change Approver and review at weekly CAB if > low risk.
- Emergency change: expedited review and retrospective.

Process (normal changes) — target review time: 5 business days
1. Create a Change Request in the Change Management system (title, owner, risk classification, rollback plan, test plan, deployment window).
2. Change Approver reviews and either greenlights or sends for CAB review.
3. If CAB required, present at next CAB meeting (weekly — Tuesdays 10:00 PT).
4. After approval, schedule deployment and notify stakeholders (routing via Redwood Console).
5. Execute change; monitor metrics and error budget.
6. Complete change ticket with post-deployment verification and link to related incident/perf dashboards.

Emergency changes:
1. Notify on-call and CAB via the incident channel.
2. Proceed with mitigation; document all steps.
3. Convene emergency CAB review within 48 hours for post-facto approval.

Rollback criteria:
- Pre-defined KPIs (error rate > 1.5x baseline, 95th latency > SLO threshold) or manual operator decision.

4) Data management
Data classification:
- Public: safe for public distribution (marketing collateral, public docs).
- Internal: company-internal operational data (internal docs, non-sensitive service metrics).
- Sensitive: PII, customer data, payment data, secrets, model training data with restrictions.
- Restricted: regulated data subject to legal controls.

Requirements by class:
- Encryption at rest and in transit for Sensitive and Restricted data.
- Access logged and retained according to retention schedule.
- Masking/obfuscation required for Sensitive data in non-production environments.

Retention and backups:
- Backups: critical production data backed up daily; backups retained for 90 days by default unless governed by contract.
- Retention schedule: see Records Retention Schedule (link).
- Data deletion: comply with legal requests and data residency controls. Requests go to Data Steward (security@redwood.ai).

Data handling checklist (example for model onboarding):
1. Document data sources and classification.
2. Confirm PII removal/approval.
3. Validate retention and access controls.
4. Run a privacy review and record in the model onboarding tracker.

Audit and monitoring:
- Data access logs forwarded to Logging Pipeline and retained per compliance requirements.
- Quarterly audit of repository permissions and S3 buckets.

5) Procurement and expenses
Procurement intake and approvals:
- All purchases must use the Procurement Request Form (Confluence) and include business justification, vendor, cost center, and expected contract term.
- Competitive procurement required for purchases > $25,000 (minimum 3 bids) unless sole-source justification documented and approved.

Purchase order and contract process:
1. Submit Procurement Request.
2. Procurement reviews vendor compliance and insurance requirements.
3. Finance issues PO after approvals.
4. Legal reviews contracts > $25,000 or with non-standard terms.

Expense reimbursement (employee travel and incidental)
- Submit expense report within 30 days using Expensify (or internal expense system).
- Required receipts for items > $25.
- Meal per diem: domestic $75/day, international $125/day.
- Hotel maximum: $300/night domestic standard; exceptions require pre-approval.
- Personal expenses (alcohol, upgrades) must be itemized and will be reviewed; company will not reimburse personal charges without prior approval.

Payment terms and vendor onboarding:
- Standard vendor payment term: Net 30.
- Vendor onboarding checklist includes insurance certificate, W-9 or W-8, security questionnaire, and PO/contract.

6) Vendor management
Onboarding checklist:
1. Fill vendor intake form and supply required documentation.
2. Security completes security questionnaire (risk assessment).
3. Legal and Procurement review contract terms.
4. Finance configures vendor in ERP for payments.
5. Assign internal vendor owner and SLAs.

Vendor risk levels and controls:
- Low risk: standard SaaS subscription with no access to sensitive data.
- Medium risk: vendor processes internal data or integrates via API; requires security questionnaire and periodic review.
- High risk: vendors handling Sensitive or Restricted data or requiring network access; require additional controls, encryption, and quarterly security attestations.

Ongoing vendor reviews:
- Annual vendor review for medium/high risk vendors.
- Quarterly billing reconciliations for all vendors > $10k/month.

Termination and offboarding:
- Ensure data return or secure deletion per contract.
- Revoke all vendor accounts and credentials within 24 hours of contract termination.
- Conduct close-out checklist: final invoice, data disposition confirmation, and access revocation evidence.

7) Travel policy (business travel)
Booking and approvals:
- All travel booked through the approved travel portal (Concur or designated partner).
- Trips > $2,000 require manager + finance pre-approval.
- Use the lowest reasonable fare; economy class for flights under 6 hours, premium economy or business requires approval.

Safety and expense guidelines:
- Keep travel receipts and submit within 30 days.
- Company will reimburse necessary business expenses; personal upgrades and side trips are employee responsibility.
- Emergency contact: people-ops@redwood.ai and security on-call.

Travel advances:
- Available for exceptional circumstances with Finance approval and reconciliation within 10 days of return.

8) Internal templates and repository
We provide standard templates to ensure consistent requests and reviewable records. All templates are stored in the Templates directory on Confluence and in the company shared drive. Key templates:
- Access Request Form (template link)
- Change Request template (fields: scope, owner, rollback, test plan)
- Procurement Request Form (PO intake)
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist
- Travel Request and Expense Template
- Data Classification and Handling Questionnaire

Usage guidance:
- Use templates verbatim for audit purposes; if modifications are required, note the change in the ticket and route to owner_team for approval.

9) Auditability and reporting
- All approvals must be recorded in the respective tooling (IAM, Change Management, Procurement, Expense system).
- Monthly compliance snapshot report prepared by Security and Finance for leadership.
- SLOs: access requests (3 business days), normal change reviews (5 business days), vendor onboarding baseline (10 business days), procurement PO issuance (7 business days).

10) Exceptions and change to these policies
- Exceptions: Must be recorded with justification, duration, and an approver from the relevant owner team and Security/Finance.
- Policy updates: people-ops maintains this document. Major policy changes require review by the leadership review board and a 14-day comment period before publishing.

Contacts and escalation
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai (policy owner)
- Security: security@redwood.ai (access, data, vendor security)
- Procurement & Finance: procurement@redwood.ai, finance@redwood.ai
- Legal: legal@redwood.ai

- Access request form: /confluence/templates/access-request
- Change request template: /confluence/templates/change-request
- Procurement intake: /confluence/templates/procurement-request
- Vendor onboarding: /confluence/templates/vendor-onboarding
